section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To whom must drivers turning left yield?
options: a:Oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right.,b:Vehicles following behind them.,c:Drivers making a right turn
note: Drivers making left turns must yield to all vehicles, bicycles, and motorcycles approaching from the opposite direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive the posted maximum speed limit?
options: a:Only under ideal driving and road conditions.,b:Only during daytime hours.,c:Only during nighttime hours.
note: The maximum posted speed is for ideal conditions; reduce speed for rain, traffic, poor visibility, or other hazards.

question: After a minor intersection collision with no injuries, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.,b:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so.,c:Leave the scene immediately.,d:Stand in traffic to warn others.
note: If there are no injuries and it's safe, move vehicles out of the travel lanes to prevent further collisions.

question: If you must park in an area not normally used for parking, what should you ensure?
options: a:Park with reverse lights on.,b:Make your vehicle visible to drivers from any direction.,c:Park five feet from the curb.,d:Leave the engine running.
note: When parked unusually, ensure your vehicle is visible to approaching drivers so it doesn't become a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, who must you yield to?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians always.,b:Oncoming traffic only if it is turning left.,c:Pedestrians only if a Walk signal is displayed.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the crosswalk before completing the turn.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Mirrors eliminate all blind spots.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:You can check blind spots using only your rearview mirror.,d:Blind spots don't exist at low speeds.
note: Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger vehicles; always be cautious when driving near them.

question: When a gate at a railroad crossing is lowering you should:
options: a:Drive around the gate.,b:Come to a complete stop and wait.,c:Speed up and cross the tracks before the gate lowers completely.
note: Do not cross when a gate is lowering; stop and wait until it is fully raised and signals have stopped.

question: Which action indicates you are driving defensively?
options: a:Keeping your eyes fixed on the vehicle directly ahead.,b:Putting one car length between you and the vehicle ahead.,c:Continuously scanning and keeping your eyes moving for hazards.
note: Defensive drivers continually scan the road and surroundings to anticipate hazards rather than staring at one spot.

question: What should you avoid doing when the road is slippery just after rain begins?
options: a:Avoid making turns and stops while driving at high speeds.,b:Test your tires' traction while going uphill.,c:Decrease the distance you look ahead of your vehicle.
note: On wet roads reduce speed and avoid sudden turns or stops to reduce the chance of skidding.

question: When is it necessary to use your low beams?
options: a:In fog, rain, snow, or mist.,b:Only on a lighted street.,c:Only on a freeway.,d:When following another vehicle at any distance.
note: Use low beams in precipitation or low visibility to reduce glare and improve visibility.

question: Which of the following is the correct practice for using your feet in driving?
options: a:Use your left foot to brake.,b:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating your vehicle.,c:You should always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.
note: Use your right foot for both the accelerator and brake for smoother and safer control of the vehicle.

question: Which headlight setting is best when driving in fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights,b:High beam headlights,c:Four-way flashers
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, or snow because high beams reflect off moisture and reduce visibility.

question: Where are a truck's blind spots typically located?
options: a:Directly behind the truck only.,b:On the immediate left of the cab only.,c:Both directly behind and on the immediate left side of the cab.,d:Only to the truck's right side.
note: Trucks have large blind spots on the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the truck where the driver cannot see smaller vehicles.

question: Driving more slowly than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:A good idea if the weather is bad.,b:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.,c:Often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can create hazards as other drivers attempt risky passes.

question: When following a school bus or a tank truck carrying hazardous materials, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:To pass them on the right.,b:To stop at all railroad crossings they must stop at.,c:To decrease your following distance.
note: School buses and tank trucks carrying hazardous cargo are required to stop at railroad crossings; be prepared to stop as well.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever acceptable to drive off the paved roadway to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Under no circumstances — do not drive off the main traveled portion to pass.,b:Only if the vehicle ahead is turning left.,c:If there are two or more lanes going your direction, you may.
note: You must not leave the paved or main-traveled portion of the road to pass another vehicle.

question: If you have had several beers, the only way to reduce the effects of alcohol is to:
options: a:Take a cold shower.,b:Wait several hours.,c:Drink several cups of coffee.
note: Time is the only means by which the body can metabolize alcohol; other methods do not speed elimination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do No Passing Zone signs indicate?
options: a:That you should speed up slightly.,b:That it is not safe to pass in the area.,c:That you should maintain your current speed.
note: A No Passing Zone sign means passing is prohibited because visibility or conditions make passing unsafe.

question: What shape/color and markings identify temporary work zone signs?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange background and black symbols or letters.,b:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.,c:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.
note: Temporary work zone signs use orange backgrounds with black text or symbols to warn of roadwork and hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do before entering the interstate?
options: a:Identify a gap in traffic, then speed up and merge when it is safe.,b:Immediately enter the far-right lane and then speed up.,c:Use the shoulder to reach freeway speed.
note: When there is no acceleration lane, wait for a sufficient gap before increasing speed and merging onto the main roadway.

question: When driving on snowy or icy roads, you should:
options: a:It is safe to use your cruise control.,b:Make speed and directional changes more gradually than you would otherwise.,c:Drive as you would under normal conditions.
note: Avoid sudden speed or directional changes on snow or ice; never use cruise control in these conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed limit on a state road in Mississippi?
options: a:70 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:40 mph.
note: The typical maximum speed on state roads is 55 mph unless signs indicate a different limit; always follow posted speeds.

question: How should you change from one lane to another?
options: a:Gradually and carefully, after checking surroundings.,b:Quickly and frequently to keep up with traffic.,c:While a vehicle is in your blind spot.
note: Change lanes only when necessary and do so gradually; always check mirrors and blind spots before moving laterally.

question: When a pedestrian guided by a dog or using a white cane is crossing, what is required of drivers?
options: a:You must always yield the right-of-way.,b:You must direct them to the nearest crosswalk.,c:You only yield if at a crosswalk corner.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians who are blind or partially sighted and who may be using a guide dog or white cane.

question: If you start feeling tired while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and either rest or change drivers.,b:Open a window and keep driving.,c:Drink caffeinated beverages and continue driving.
note: To avoid drowsy driving, take breaks or switch drivers; short-term fixes like caffeine are not reliably safe for long trips.

question: Why should you use headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?
options: a:To keep your engine warm.,b:So others can see your vehicle.,c:To warn others of bad weather conditions.
note: If visibility is reduced by weather, turning on low beam headlights makes your vehicle easier for others to see.

question: How must you respond when you encounter a pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog?
options: a:Yell for them to move along.,b:Yield the right-of-way and allow them to cross safely.,c:Proceed if they are not in your lane.
note: Blind or partially blind pedestrians using a cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way; take every precaution and let them cross safely before proceeding.

question: In foggy conditions, what should you do about your headlights and speed?
options: a:Use high beams and maintain speed.,b:Slow down and use low beam headlights.,c:Increase speed to clear the fog quickly.,d:Use parking lights only.
note: Use low beams and reduce speed in fog; if visibility is extremely poor, pull off the road safely.

question: What is the best preventive measure to avoid dangerous driving situations?
options: a:Constantly be aware of what is happening around your vehicle.,b:Turn off the radio to eliminate distractions.,c:Keep your eyes focused only on the road immediately ahead.
note: Scanning the road and surroundings front, sides, and rear helps you detect hazards early and respond safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.,b:Yield to vehicles only on your right.,c:Should slow down but never stop.
note: Approach a yield sign prepared to stop and give the right-of-way to traffic that would conflict with your intended movement.

question: If a steady green light turns yellow and you are already in the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Increase speed to clear the intersection.,b:Stop immediately.,c:Clear the intersection safely and promptly.,d:Back up slowly.
note: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue and clear it as safely as possible.

question: What is the best action if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Stop to rest or change drivers.,b:Open a window and continue driving.,c:Drink coffee and keep driving.
note: Fatigue impairs judgment and reaction time — stop in a safe place to rest or switch drivers if possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful regarding passing?
options: a:Passing in any marked no passing zone.,b:Passing over a railroad crossing.,c:Both passing in no passing zones and over railroad crossings are illegal.
note: You may not pass where signs or lines prohibit it, including no passing zones and at or on railroad crossings; both actions are illegal.

question: What problems can a worn suspension cause?
options: a:Vehicle control problems, making the car harder to steer and less stable.,b:Squealing brakes only.,c:Excess slack in the steering column only.
note: A faulty suspension reduces vehicle stability and control and should be repaired to maintain safe handling.

question: If a lane has an overhead sign showing an arrow with the word ONLY, what must you do?
options: a:Travel only in the direction shown by the arrow.,b:Always change lanes when you see this sign.,c:Look for a destination sign to decide where to go.
note: A lane control sign with an arrow and ONLY restricts you to the indicated movement from that lane.

question: Slowing down just to look at crashes or unusual events:
options: a:Causes traffic congestion.,b:Prevents rear-end collisions.,c:Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.
note: Avoid 'rubbernecking' because it causes slowdowns and congestion and increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn not permitted?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.
note: Never attempt a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where oncoming traffic or pedestrians may be hidden.

question: What is the only thing that reduces blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and alcohol's effects on the body?
options: a:Drinking caffeine,b:Eating foods high in fat,c:Time
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and remove alcohol; nothing else speeds this process.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what is the proper procedure?
options: a:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if it is safe to do so.,b:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first passing car.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get attention.
note: If you stop on the shoulder, use hazard lights and remain in the vehicle when possible; walking alongside a high-speed roadway is dangerous.

question: Where should drivers be especially alert to children?
options: a:School zones and playgrounds, residential neighborhoods, and other areas where children gather.,b:Only at marked school crossings.,c:Only residential neighborhoods.,d:Only playgrounds.
note: Be cautious in all places where children may be present: school zones, playgrounds, and residential areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow is displayed with a red traffic light, when may you proceed in the arrow’s direction?
options: a:If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear, you may proceed.,b:Only after coming to a complete stop first.,c:You must wait until the main light turns green.
note: A green arrow grants permission to move in its direction; yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection first.

question: When should you avoid using your horn?
options: a:When visibility ahead is limited.,b:Near blind pedestrians.,c:If you might hit another vehicle.,d:To warn a car about to hit you.
note: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians; it may startle them or endanger them.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only if they are in a crosswalk.,b:At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.,c:Only if the traffic lights favor the pedestrian.
note: Always yield to pedestrians when necessary to avoid striking them, regardless of who is violating a law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers respond to a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Treat it as a stop sign and come to a complete stop.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Proceed since you have the right-of-way.,d:Stop only if other vehicles are present.
note: A flashing red light means stop completely before proceeding, like a stop sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed limit on a rural interstate?
options: a:70 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:40 mph.
note: The typical maximum speed on rural interstates in Mississippi is 70 mph unless signs indicate otherwise.

question: When exiting a freeway on a downhill ramp that curves, how should you handle your speed?
options: a:Slow to a safe speed before you enter the curve.,b:Wait until you've entered the curve to begin braking.,c:Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curved exit ramp to maintain control; braking in a curve increases skid risk.

question: When during rainy weather should you be most cautious when turning or stopping?
options: a:After it has been raining all day.,b:One half hour after it stops raining.,c:During the first half hour of rain.
note: Road surfaces can be especially slippery during the first half hour of rain as water mixes with oil and residues on the pavement.

question: What important step should you take before making a turn?
options: a:Check traffic in all directions and adjust speed.,b:Increase your speed to make the turn quicker.,c:Move toward the left lane regardless of direction.
note: Before turning, look behind and to both sides to ensure it is safe and alter your speed as needed to complete the turn safely.

question: If weather or light conditions require lights, which should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:High beam headlights.,d:Interior dome light.
note: Use low beam headlights in bad weather or reduced visibility; high beams can cause glare.

question: When following a motorcycle, you should leave extra space in front of your vehicle when following:
options: a:Motorcycle,b:Station wagon,c:Passenger vehicle
note: Motorcycles can stop or change speed quickly and are harder to see; allow extra following distance.

question: How should drivers approach a curve in the road?
options: a:Decrease their speed before entering the curve.,b:Increase speed to maintain momentum.,c:Maintain their normal speed.
note: Slow down before entering a curve to maintain control; accelerate again only after passing the curve's midpoint if safe.

question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,b:Lanes move in the same direction and passing prohibited.,c:Passing allowed from both directions.,d:Passing allowed only during daytime.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and prohibit passing from either direction.

question: Are you required to obey directions given by a school crossing guard?
options: a:Only during school hours.,b:At all times when they are directing traffic.,c:Only if you see children present.
note: Drivers must always obey crossing guards near schools; their directions help protect children crossing the street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If someone is merging into your lane on the freeway, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Maintain your position and speed at all costs.,b:Make room for the merging vehicle if it is safe to do so.,c:Speed up to prevent them from merging.,d:Brake sharply to let them in.
note: When traffic allows, make room to allow vehicles to merge safely into your lane.

question: At a flashing yellow traffic signal, what should you do as you approach?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop before crossing the intersection.,c:Wait for a green light before moving.
note: A flashing yellow signal warns drivers to slow, look, and proceed carefully through the intersection.

question: What can happen if you take prescription medication while drinking alcohol?
options: a:It can make you unfit to drive safely.,b:It will likely make you more alert.,c:There will likely be no effect on driving ability.
note: Alcohol combined with many medications can greatly increase impairment and make driving unsafe.

question: If a large truck or bus is turning right where you also intend to turn, what should you do?
options: a:Try to cut in front of it before it completes its turn.,b:Wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn.,c:Squeeze between the vehicle and the curb.
note: Large trucks and buses need extra space to complete turns; wait until they finish before making your turn to avoid collisions.

question: What danger does driver fatigue most increase?
options: a:Missing an exit.,b:Being late for appointments.,c:Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.
note: Fatigue impairs judgment, slows reactions, and can cause drivers to fall asleep, greatly increasing crash risk.

question: What color and background do temporary construction signs have?
options: a:Red background with green writing.,b:Orange background with black writing.,c:Yellow background with blue writing.
note: Temporary signs in work and construction zones use orange backgrounds with black text or symbols to warn drivers of changes and hazards.

question: Why should motorists leave extra space for children riding bicycles?
options: a:They are smaller and more difficult to see than adults,b:Both that they lack adult reflexes and are harder to see,c:Children always follow traffic rules,d:They do not have the same reflexes as adults
note: Children are smaller, less predictable, and have slower reactions than adults. Give them extra room and be especially cautious near schools and parks.

question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection?
options: a:Stop before crossing.,b:Slow down and cross carefully when safe.,c:Wait for the green light.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution; slow down and be alert for other vehicles and pedestrians.

question: Which describes how defensive drivers think?
options: a:They know other drivers will do the right thing.,b:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.,c:They expect no breaks and give none.
note: Defensive drivers anticipate others' mistakes and are prepared to respond safely.

question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic signal require drivers to do?
options: a:Proceed in the arrow's direction after yielding.,b:Stop and remain stopped; do not move in the arrow's direction.,c:Slow and proceed with caution.,d:Turn only after signaling.
note: A steady red arrow means traffic in that lane must not proceed in the arrow's direction; wait for a green signal.

question: What does excessive speed most often lead to?
options: a:High-risk decision-making and an increased chance of crashes.,b:An improved ability to react to hazards.,c:Saving a significant amount of travel time.
note: Speeding is a leading factor in crashes — it reduces reaction time and increases severity of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do?
options: a:Increase your speed to clear the intersection,b:You may continue through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear,c:Stop and yield to vehicles on the left,d:Only turn right on green
note: A steady green light means you may go through the intersection, but you must yield to pedestrians and any traffic already in the intersection.

question: How can you prevent hydroplaning in wet weather?
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,b:Slow down.,c:Move to the shoulder when it starts to rain.,d:Increase your speed slightly.
note: Hydroplaning risk is reduced by lowering speed on wet pavement; do not use cruise control in heavy rain.

question: How should you steer and brake when driving in inclement weather?
options: a:Steer and brake smoothly,b:Steer off the road immediately,c:Drive only in low gear,d:Brake and turn abruptly to correct slides
note: In bad weather, use smooth steering and gentle braking to maintain control and reduce the chance of skids or loss of control.

question: As you near the crest of a hill, how should you drive?
options: a:Speed up slightly to crests quickly.,b:Be prepared to stop if necessary.,c:Maintain a steady speed at all times.
note: Do not assume the road ahead is clear; adjust speed so you can stop if a stalled vehicle or hazard appears over the hill.

question: If poor weather reduces your visibility, you should:
options: a:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,b:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Increase following distance to give yourself more time to react when visibility is reduced by weather.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, where should your vehicle be positioned?
options: a:Near the right-hand side of the road.,b:Near the centerline or lane closest to the centerline.,c:On the left of the centerline.
note: Begin a left turn from the lane nearest the centerline and enter the first available legal lane of the street you are turning into.

question: In a work zone, how should you drive?
options: a:Increase your speed to get through quickly.,b:Reduce speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,c:Maintain your usual speed throughout the zone.
note: Slow down, obey posted limits, and be prepared to stop for changing conditions and workers in work zones.

question: When backing up, what is the recommended way to view behind you?
options: a:Look through the rear window while moving slowly.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Press hard on the gas to get out quickly.,d:Rely only on a backup camera.
note: When reversing, look directly through the rear window, keep speed low, and use mirrors and cameras as supplements.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but don't see a gap in traffic, what should you do on the ramp?
options: a:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Maintain speed and force a gap.
note: If no opening exists, slow down on the entrance ramp to wait for a safe gap so you can accelerate to highway speed before merging.

question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on a city street?
options: a:To spot potential hazards earlier.,b:Because the speed limit is always higher.,c:To be able to change lanes more often.
note: On freeways you need to watch further ahead to detect changes in traffic, merging vehicles, and rapidly changing road conditions so you can react in time.

question: If you expect to be struck from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Release your seat belt.,b:Brace yourself against the seatback.,c:Press your head against the head restraint.
note: Do not release your seat belt; brace against the seat back and press your head to the head restraint to reduce whiplash injuries.

question: Where are high-beam headlights appropriate?
options: a:When within 500 feet of another vehicle.,b:On open country roads with no nearby traffic.,c:In heavy city traffic.,d:In foggy conditions.
note: Use high beams on open roads where no other vehicles are nearby; reduce speed at night.

question: If you want to pass a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.,b:Keep driving at a steady speed; the oncoming vehicle must stop for you.,c:Honk your horn to get the pedestrian to move over.
note: Handle one hazard at a time: let the oncoming vehicle pass, then pass the pedestrian only if it is safe.

question: If your vehicle's wheels drop off the pavement edge, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce speed, check traffic, and when safe gradually steer back onto the road.,b:Turn sharply back onto the roadway immediately.,c:Stop and wait on the shoulder.
note: Do not try to jerk back onto the pavement; slow, signal, check traffic, and re-enter smoothly when safe.

question: If oncoming headlights are dazzling you at night, how should you respond?
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of the road and avoid looking directly at the lights.,b:Switch your headlights to high beams.,c:Turn your headlights off and on repeatedly.
note: Looking toward the right edge reduces glare and helps keep your car safely on course until you pass.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how should you adjust your following distance?
options: a:Follow closer than you would a passenger car.,b:Allow more distance than you would for a passenger vehicle.,c:Drive to the truck's right and wait to pass.
note: Large trucks have larger blind spots and longer stopping distances, so follow farther behind than you would behind a car.

question: What qualifies as a driving distraction?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Only electronic devices that you use while driving.,c:Only passengers who shout or cause evasive action.
note: Distractions include anything that diverts attention from driving — visual, manual, or cognitive tasks increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the interstate, after checking for a gap and signaling, what should you do?
options: a:Expect traffic to allow you into the lane because you have the right-of-way.,b:Merge carefully into the gap when it is safe.,c:Wait until the lane clears entirely before merging.
note: Accelerate to match traffic speed and merge carefully into a gap when it is safe; do not assume others will make room for you.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:Hazard flashers only.
note: Use low beams in fog; high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: If you see pedestrians close to the roadway where you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain speed,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly,c:Slow down and pass with caution
note: When pedestrians are near the road, reduce speed and be prepared to stop to avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you park facing downhill on a two-way road with no curb, how should you point your front wheels?
options: a:Left, toward the center of the road,b:Right, toward the side of the road,c:Straight ahead
note: When parking downhill on a roadway without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, you should never:
options: a:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.,b:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,c:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously.
note: Avoid abrupt lane changes; always check mirrors and blind spots and signal before moving.

question: Which roadway feature tends to freeze before surrounding pavement?
options: a:A tunnel.,b:An intersection.,c:A bridge or overpass.
note: Bridges and overpasses are exposed to air both above and below and often freeze before the adjacent roadway.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you start driving, after positioning your seat.,b:Before you get into the car, while outside it.,c:Only when you need to use them while driving.
note: Adjust mirrors before you move the vehicle so you have maximum visibility from the start of your trip.

question: Approaching an intersection where the traffic signal is steady yellow and you have not entered the intersection, you should:
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow warns the signal is about to turn red; if you can do so safely, come to a controlled stop.

question: If a tire blows out, what should you do first?
options: a:Apply the brake and hold it.,b:Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.,c:Pull over quickly.
note: Keep a firm grip, steer straight, ease off the gas, and apply brakes gently as you slow to a safe stop off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived before you.,b:The driver on your left.,c:The driver across from you.,d:The driver who signals first.
note: Vehicles at a four-way stop proceed in the order they arrive; yield to drivers who arrived before you.

question: As your travel speed increases, what should you do to remain safe?
options: a:Look well ahead of your vehicle.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Change lanes more often.,d:Reduce following distance.
note: At higher speeds, look farther ahead to give yourself time to react to hazards.

question: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:
options: a:There isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.,b:The railroad crossing is located in a city or town that has frequent train traffic.,c:You are transporting two or more young children in a passenger vehicle.
note: If you cannot clear the tracks completely, wait until there is enough space beyond the tracks so you will not be stuck on them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a left-turn lane for an upcoming left turn and there is oncoming traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.,b:Signal before you arrive at the intersection.,c:Move to the left of the center lane.
note: Signal well before the turn and keep your wheels straight until you begin the turn to avoid being pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: When visibility is reduced by fog, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the road and stop if visibility is too poor,b:Slow down and use your low beam headlights,c:Use your high beam headlights,d:Flash your headlights to warn others
note: Slow down and use low beams in fog; if you cannot see safely, pull off the road and wait until conditions improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When facing a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.,b:Proceed because you have the right-of-way.,c:Force pedestrians to yield to your vehicle.,d:Honk to move pedestrians faster.
note: You must yield to pedestrians who are crossing when you face a green light, especially if turning.

question: How can you stay aware of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn and look out your back window while driving.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots at all times.
note: Regularly scanning your rearview mirror helps you monitor traffic behind you and anticipate problems.

question: You must give the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:
options: a:In a marked crosswalk.,b:In any crosswalk or intersection.,c:Crossing any street.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the street in marked or unmarked crosswalks and should yield to anyone crossing the street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view is blocked at an intersection, how should you proceed?
options: a:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.,b:Slow down and look both ways without stopping.,c:Maintain your speed and quickly look both ways.
note: Come to a stop and slowly creep forward until you have a clear view of cross traffic before entering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Both when a police officer orders you to stop and at a red traffic light.,b:Only at a red traffic light.,c:Only when an officer orders you to stop.
note: You must obey both traffic control devices such as red lights and lawful orders from officers directing traffic.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, what is the correct response?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly to regain traction.,b:Slow down gradually and avoid braking.,c:Speed up to get through the water faster.,d:Turn the steering wheel sharply.
note: When hydroplaning, ease off the accelerator and do not apply the brakes; allow the vehicle to slow naturally.

question: When parking uphill where there is no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn wheels toward the edge of the road.,b:Turn wheels away from the edge of the road.,c:Keep wheels pointing straight ahead.
note: On an uphill without a curb, turn the wheels toward the edge so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

question: How should you behave when encountering a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog crossing the street?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the person is well away from your path of travel.,b:Carefully drive around them while they are crossing.,c:Sound your horn as you pass to alert them.
note: Blind pedestrians always have the right-of-way; stop and wait until they are safely out of your path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When completing a pass, when should you return to your previous lane?
options: a:When you can see the entire vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.,b:When you sense you are far enough ahead of the other vehicle.,c:When the other driver signals for you to return.
note: Only move back when a full view of the passed vehicle is visible in your mirror and the path is clear.

question: Who may legally use marked handicap parking spaces?
options: a:Only drivers or passengers with the appropriate license plate or hanging placard.,b:Anyone when other spaces are full.,c:People who claim they do not feel well that day.
note: Handicap parking is reserved for those with state-authorized plates or placards; misuse may result in fines.

question: What happens as your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases?
options: a:You become more coordinated.,b:You become more intoxicated and impaired.,c:You become more alert.,d:Your reaction times improve.
note: A higher BAC indicates greater impairment of judgment, coordination, and reaction time.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, what action may be necessary immediately?
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn to warn and stop the child.,b:Flash your headlights to get their attention.,c:Start to prepare to slow down only.
note: If a child steps toward the street, a quick horn blast can warn and prevent them from entering the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you make room for vehicles entering the freeway?
options: a:Slowing down or adjusting speed.,b:Maintaining your speed and position at all times.,c:Honk at the entering drivers to make them wait.
note: If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to create a gap for entering vehicles; merge when safe to do so.

question: What color are temporary construction and maintenance warning devices?
options: a:Orange,b:Yellow,c:Red
note: Work zone signs, cones, and barriers are orange; exercise extra caution when you see them.

question: Blue roadway signs provide information about:
options: a:Motorist services.,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Mileage information, such as distances to specific locations.
note: Blue signs are service signs that indicate things like rest areas, food, gas, and hospitals.

question: Which headlights should you use in fog, heavy rain, or snow?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Fog lights only without headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog, heavy rain, and snow; high beams can reflect and reduce your visibility.

question: What term describes the amount of alcohol present in a person's bloodstream?
options: a:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC),b:Implied consent (IC),c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC)
note: BAC is the standard measurement for alcohol in the blood and is used to determine impairment and legal limits.

question: The driver in front of you has stopped at a crosswalk. What is your required action?
options: a:Cautiously pass at 10 mph or slower.,b:Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have cleared.,c:Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle.
note: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk; there may be pedestrians you cannot see. Wait until the crosswalk is clear.

question: If the rear of your vehicle skids to the left, what steering action should you take?
options: a:Steer to the left,b:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral,c:Steer to the right,d:Pump the brakes rapidly
note: In a skid, take your foot off the pedals and steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go to help regain control.

question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Relax, concentrate on driving, and be realistic about travel time.,b:Tailgate slow drivers to encourage them to speed up.,c:Drive above the posted limit to avoid delays.,d:Use gestures to communicate frustration.
note: Prevent aggression by staying calm, planning time, obeying speed limits, and not taking others' actions personally.

question: What is the only effective method to remove alcohol from your system?
options: a:Wait — allow time for your body to metabolize the alcohol.,b:Drink strong coffee to sober up quickly.,c:Take a cold shower to remove alcohol effects.
note: Time is the only thing that lowers BAC; remedies like coffee or showers do not speed alcohol elimination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you pass a vehicle on the right by using the shoulder?
options: a:If the shoulder is paved and it's safe.,b:When the car ahead is driving too slowly.,c:Never drive off the pavement onto the shoulder to pass.,d:Whenever traffic is slow.
note: You must not drive off the pavement or onto the shoulder to pass; pass on the right only when safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you start into an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red?
options: a:No — never enter if you will block the intersection.,b:Only if you entered on a yellow light.,c:Only if you entered on a green light.,d:Yes, if you have the right-of-way.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it; blocking intersections is prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and not already in it, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a safe stop if possible.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Maintain your speed and proceed through.
note: A steady yellow warns that the light will soon turn red — prepare to stop safely if you have not entered the intersection.

question: When you approach a stopped school bus with its lights flashing and arm extended, you should:
options: a:Stop.,b:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are present.,c:Proceed at normal speed, but watch for children.
note: You must stop and remain stopped until the bus retracts the arm and turns off the flashing red lights.

question: When is it legal to go around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Never — you must not go around or under any lowered gate.,b:When the lights are not flashing.,c:When you can see clearly in both directions.
note: Never drive around or under a lowered gate; wait until the gate is fully raised and the track is clear.

question: It is very foggy. What should you do with your lights?
options: a:Turn on your emergency flashers.,b:Use high beam headlights.,c:Use low beam headlights.,d:Turn off all lights to avoid glare.
note: Use low beams in fog; high beams will reflect back and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging into traffic from a curb or parked position, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for a large enough gap so you can accelerate to the speed of traffic before merging.,b:Drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet after merging.,c:Wait for the first two vehicles to pass and then move into the lane.
note: Always wait for a gap that allows you to reach the flow of traffic without forcing others to slow or swerve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed limit in a school zone?
options: a:15 miles per hour,b:20 miles per hour,c:30 miles per hour
note: School zone speed limits are often reduced (commonly 15 mph) to protect children; obey posted limits and signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate highway you should:
options: a:Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.,b:Always stop before entering the highway.,c:Merge across two lanes at once.
note: Choose an appropriate gap in traffic on the main roadway and merge smoothly at the speed of traffic.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicate?
options: a:Centerline separates opposing traffic,b:Do not pass,c:Reduce your speed,d:Traffic signal ahead
note: A solid yellow line on your side means passing is prohibited from your lane. If both yellow lines are solid, neither direction may pass.

question: How must you yield to an emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights?
options: a:Drive as close to the right edge and stop, taking care not to stop in an intersection.,b:Pull into the right lane and slow until it has passed.,c:Stop immediately even if you are in the middle of an intersection.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, move to the right edge of the road and stop out of intersections until it has passed.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:Only when slowing down.,b:Often to monitor traffic behind you.,c:Only before changing lanes.,d:Never; mirrors distract you.
note: Frequently check your rearview mirrors so you know how traffic is moving behind you and can react appropriately.

question: When a school bus ahead is stopped with red lights flashing and its stop arm extended, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop until all the children have left the bus.,b:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,c:Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus cautiously.
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights and the stop arm is out, motorists must stop until the lights are off and the arm is retracted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you in a no passing zone, how should you respond?
options: a:Pull completely off the road.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Slow down and allow the passing vehicle to re-enter your lane safely.
note: When being passed, slow down and make it easier for the other driver to return to the travel lane safely.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops directly in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.,b:Large trucks and buses require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.,c:Large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds than small vehicles.
note: Large vehicles need greater stopping distance due to their size and weight; sudden stops in front of them increase collision risk.

question: If the centerline is a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is on your side, what does that mean?
options: a:You may pass other vehicles to the left when it is safe.,b:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,c:You may only turn right.,d:You must merge immediately.
note: When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may pass into the oncoming lane to pass if it's clear and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into any available lane.,b:Into the first lane in the direction of travel.,c:Into the second lane from the curb.
note: When turning from a two-way onto a one-way street, turn into the first lane available in the direction you are heading.

question: If you see a person using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, what is required of you?
options: a:The pedestrian must yield to traffic.,b:You must yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.,c:Flash your headlights to warn them.
note: Pedestrians who are blind or partially sighted and are using a cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way; always be courteous and wait until they finish crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, which action is prohibited?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and find an alternate route.,b:Proceed to the next exit and return to your intended exit via surface streets.,c:Back up on the roadway or shoulder to reach the missed exit.
note: Never back up on the freeway or shoulder after missing an exit; continue to the next exit and safely re-route.

question: How are bicycles treated when using the roadway?
options: a:Are considered vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.,b:Do not follow specific rules of the road.,c:Must always yield the right-of-way to motor vehicles.
note: Bicyclists on the road have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers and should be respected accordingly.

question: If you parallel park facing downhill, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels toward the curb or side of the road.,b:Turn the wheels away from the curb.,c:Keep the wheels straight.,d:Turn the wheels toward traffic flow.
note: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb so the vehicle will stop against it if it moves.

question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow on a traffic signal signify?
options: a:Drivers should immediately stop and remain stopped.,b:The protected left turn is ending and you should prepare to yield.,c:The left turn will remain protected indefinitely.
note: A yellow arrow indicates the protected left-turn phase is ending; drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic when it ends.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and the driver on your left arrive at a four-way stop simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You — the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,c:Whoever is signaling to turn has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right goes first; yield if you are to the left.

question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Whenever yielding helps prevent a collision.,b:Never; always assert your right-of-way.,c:Often even at controlled intersections.,d:Only to emergency vehicles.
note: Yield your right-of-way when doing so helps prevent crashes, even if you technically have the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What important step must you take before passing on a two-lane road?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles to ensure safe clearance.,b:Sound your horn continuously.,c:Flash headlights at the vehicle ahead.,d:Pass without checking mirrors.
note: Ensure there is enough time and space to pass safely by judging oncoming traffic and distance.

question: What color are most regulatory traffic signs?
options: a:White,b:Green,c:Yellow
note: Regulatory signs (speed limits, directions, no-turns, etc.) are typically white rectangles or squares with black or red symbols or lettering.

question: In a vehicle with airbags, the safest place for children age 12 and under is:
options: a:The front seat.,b:The back seat.,c:The bed of a pick-up truck.
note: Children 12 and under should ride in the back seat because airbags can be dangerous to small passengers.

question: When an oncoming vehicle has bright headlights at night, how should you avoid being blinded?
options: a:Stop until the vehicle passes.,b:Look toward the right edge of your lane.,c:Look directly at the oncoming headlights.,d:Flash your high beams.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights.

question: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately in the intersection and wait.,b:Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.,c:Pull to the right side of the intersection and stop.,d:Speed up and get out of the way.
note: If in an intersection, clear it and then pull to the right and stop to yield to emergency vehicles.

question: Any amount of alcohol in the bloodstream can affect a driver's:
options: a:Knowledge of traffic laws.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Right-of-way privileges only.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair judgment and coordination, increasing the risk of crashes and legal consequences.

question: How can you avoid losing traction on wet roads?
options: a:Make abrupt turns.,b:Slow down.,c:Apply the brakes firmly.,d:Use cruise control.
note: Reduce speed on wet roads to prevent hydroplaning; maintain tires and avoid sudden inputs.

question: A broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction when safe.,b:A construction zone is ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Broken yellow centerlines indicate passing is allowed when no oncoming traffic and it is safe to do so.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Applying your brakes when possible.,b:Letting go of the steering wheel.,c:Pressing your head against the head restraint.
note: Do not release the steering wheel; brace yourself by holding the wheel, pressing your head to the restraint, and be ready to apply brakes to avoid secondary collisions.

question: If you are angry after an argument, what is the safest action before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down and cool off before you drive.,b:Loudly play the radio while driving to distract yourself.,c:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.
note: Strong emotions impair concentration and judgment; give yourself time to calm before getting behind the wheel.

question: What speed should you choose relative to road and weather conditions?
options: a:A speed appropriate for the current road and weather conditions.,b:Always at the posted speed limit.,c:Always at the speed of surrounding vehicles.
note: Adjust your speed to match visibility, road surface, traffic, and weather — never exceed posted limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving too slowly is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.,c:The speed you drive does not affect safety.
note: Driving well below the normal speed of traffic can cause congestion and risky passing maneuvers by others.

question: After a train passes and you have stopped at a crossing, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Wait for signal lights to stop flashing.,b:Look for a second train.,c:Both of the above.
note: Make sure all warning signals have stopped and check for another approaching train before crossing.

question: At a flashing red traffic signal, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed when clear.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the light stops flashing.
note: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign: stop fully, yield to others, and go only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, what is allowed?
options: a:You must stay within your lane,b:You may cross the centerline to change lanes,c:You may change lanes only from the left lane,d:You may cross only to pass large vehicles
note: Broken white lines separate lanes going in the same direction and may be crossed when it is safe to change lanes.

question: Alcohol in any concentration is classified as what?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A depressant.,c:Neither a stimulant nor depressant.,d:A performance enhancer.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant that impairs judgment, coordination, and reaction time.

question: How does excessive speed affect crash severity?
options: a:It increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.,b:It saves time and usually improves safety.,c:It helps you maneuver around obstacles more easily.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and the force of impact, raising the risk of severe injury or death.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren is approaching you, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving but stay out of its path.,b:Pull over toward the right edge of the road and stop.,c:Try to reach your destination before it catches up to you.
note: Mississippi law requires drivers to yield to emergency vehicles by pulling as far to the right as possible and stopping; if in an intersection, clear it before pulling over.

question: If driving on a highway next to a single broken white line, what are you allowed to do?
options: a:Cross the line to pass or change lanes when safe.,b:Never cross the line.,c:Cross only to make right turns.,d:Cross only during daytime.
note: A dashed white line separates same-direction lanes and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you return to your original lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,c:When you are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.
note: Ensure there is enough space by verifying you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your mirror before returning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass a vehicle on the road?
options: a:When a solid center line is next to your lane.,b:When there is a broken center line next to your lane.,c:On a hill or curve where you cannot see ahead.
note: A broken center line indicates passing is permitted when it is safe to do so; do not pass where a solid line is next to your lane or where visibility is restricted.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct action?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Apply the brakes lightly.,c:Stay off the brakes.
note: If the vehicle skids, avoid braking; steer to regain control and only use brakes lightly if needed once stabilized.

question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:The driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.,b:You signal your intention for three seconds.,c:You can see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Only return when you can clearly see the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror, indicating sufficient space.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, which lights should be used?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beams.,c:Parking lights.,d:Interior dome lights.
note: Low beam headlights improve visibility to others and reduce glare in rain or fog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed and hope traffic clears quickly.,b:Stay out of the intersection until traffic ahead clears.,c:Turn left to find another route immediately.
note: Do not enter an intersection you cannot clear; remain stopped until the roadway ahead is free to avoid blocking cross traffic.

question: What does a red arrow pointing to the right mean?
options: a:Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.,b:Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.,c:Turn in that direction after you come to a complete stop.
note: A red arrow is a stop signal for the indicated direction; do not turn against it until a green light or arrow appears.

question: What does an orange-and-red triangular emblem on the back of a slow vehicle mean?
options: a:The vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle and travels at lower speeds.,b:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:There is shoulder work ahead.
note: A reflective orange-red triangle marks vehicles that are designed to operate at slower speeds, like farm equipment.

question: When should you allow extra following distance behind another vehicle?
options: a:When following a small passenger car,b:When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle,c:When following a station wagon,d:When following a motorcycle
note: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles or drivers who cannot see you, since they may not be able to stop or maneuver safely.

question: What do yellow centerlines on the road mark?
options: a:The separation of traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,b:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,c:Carpool lanes separated from regular lanes.
note: Yellow lines indicate the center of a two-way roadway; they separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:
options: a:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.,b:At all times.,c:Only if a crossing guard is present.
note: Pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog must always be given the right-of-way.

question: If another driver is acting aggressively toward you, how should you respond?
options: a:Get out of their way and avoid confrontation.,b:Challenge them to establish right-of-way.,c:Speed up to put distance between you immediately.
note: Do not engage or escalate; safely yield or change lanes to avoid conflict and reduce crash risk.

question: When visibility is reduced by fog, which headlights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers only.
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, or snow; high beams can reflect back and worsen visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Leave the front wheels straight.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb so the car will roll into the curb if the brakes fail.

question: What is the correct mindset when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Expect the unexpected and drive with extra caution.,b:Slightly increase your speed to clear the zone.,c:Expect workers to yield to motorists.,d:Ignore signs and maintain your normal driving.
note: Construction zones have changing conditions; reduce speed and be prepared for sudden changes.

question: Like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness can:
options: a:Help you to be a better driver.,b:Make you feel better.,c:Impair your judgment.
note: Fatigue reduces reaction time and impairs judgement, increasing the risk of crashes similar to intoxication.

question: Collisions are more likely when which condition exists?
options: a:All vehicles travel at about the same speed.,b:One vehicle travels much faster or slower than surrounding traffic.,c:Everyone follows the flow of traffic.,d:Weather is perfect.
note: A vehicle traveling at a significantly different speed from the flow of traffic increases collision risk.

question: On the freeway behind a large truck, how should you follow?
options: a:Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead than you can.,b:Farther behind the truck than you would when following a passenger vehicle.,c:No more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.
note: Maintain increased following distance behind large trucks to allow additional stopping time and visibility.

question: What is the purpose of broken yellow lines on highways?
options: a:They separate lanes of traffic traveling in opposite directions and indicate passing is permitted.,b:They separate lanes moving in the same direction.,c:They indicate no passing zones.,d:They mark the road edge.
note: Broken yellow lines separate opposite-direction lanes; dashed lines mean passing is allowed when safe.

question: How is a crosswalk defined?
options: a:A type of four-way intersection.,b:An area set aside for road workers.,c:An area designated for pedestrian crossing of the roadway.
note: A crosswalk marks the area where pedestrians may cross; it can be marked by painted lines or be unmarked at an intersection.

question: Which of the following is true about impairment from alcohol and drugs?
options: a:They only affect alertness and concentration.,b:They only affect reaction time and coordination.,c:They affect alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination.
note: Alcohol and many drugs depress the nervous system and impair multiple driving skills including alertness, reaction time, and coordination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After about three seconds have passed.,c:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: Only move back when you can clearly see the passed vehicle's front end in your mirror and you have checked blind spots.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you do?
options: a:Blow your horn to make the rider move to the shoulder,b:Remain in the same lane because the motorcycle is small,c:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass,d:Pass using only part of the motorcycle's lane
note: Give a motorcycle a full lane when passing; never crowd or share the lane, and do not return to your lane too soon.

question: On a slippery road, your following distance should be:
options: a:Closer to the car ahead than normal.,b:Farther from the car ahead than normal.,c:No different than normal.
note: Reduce speed and increase following distance on slippery surfaces because braking distances are longer.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, how should you adjust your speed?
options: a:Slow enough to stop within the area your headlights illuminate.,b:Turn on high beams to better see ahead.,c:Keep instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to others.
note: Drive at a speed that allows you to stop within the distance illuminated by your headlights to account for limited nighttime visibility.

question: What should you do before entering a curve?
options: a:Reduce your speed to a safe level for the curve.,b:Activate your turn signal before the curve.,c:Brake hard as you enter the curve.
note: Slow down before a curve to avoid losing control; avoid heavy braking while turning.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.,b:Call your insurance company when you get home.,c:Wait for the owner to return.
note: If you damage a parked vehicle or other property, leave a note with your name, phone number, and address securely attached to the vehicle or property.

question: Which lights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Fog lights,b:Low beam headlights,c:Parking lights,d:High beam headlights
note: Use low beam headlights in fog; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility and make it harder to see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed repeatedly on the right and left while driving in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in the center lane regardless.,b:Move to the lane on your right when safe.,c:Move to the lane on your left immediately.
note: On multi-lane roads, drive in the right lanes unless passing or turning; if traffic is passing you frequently, move right when safe.

question: What is the purpose of barriers, drums, cones, and signs in a work zone?
options: a:To annoy drivers with slow traffic.,b:To inconvenience travelers.,c:To keep traffic away from hazardous work areas and protect workers.
note: Work zone devices channel traffic and warn drivers to protect workers and equipment; obey all signs and reduced speed limits.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use only the lap belt.,b:Use both the lap and shoulder belts together.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.
note: Use both lap and shoulder belts for proper protection; relying on only one part greatly reduces effectiveness.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:Another vehicle is in your way.,b:When it may help prevent a collision.,c:Another driver makes a mistake.
note: Use your horn only to warn others of danger or to help avoid collisions, not to express frustration.

question: How can sudden wind gusts on highways affect vehicles?
options: a:They only affect large vehicles.,b:They can create problems for all vehicles.,c:They only cause visibility problems.,d:They have no impact on vehicle control.
note: Strong gusts can affect vehicles of all sizes by reducing stability and moving vehicles off course.

question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c:All of the above.
note: Many prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs can impair driving; read labels and avoid driving if impaired.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams at night, how should you respond?
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of your lane and watch the vehicle from the corner of your eye.,b:Look ahead toward the left edge of your lane.,c:Keep looking straight ahead in your lane.
note: Avoid staring at the blinding lights; look toward the right side of your lane and monitor the car peripherally.

question: Which of these is a recommended safe driving habit?
options: a:Using high beams in fog.,b:Checking rearview mirrors frequently.,c:Staring constantly at the road ahead.,d:Driving without signaling.
note: To stay aware of hazards, scan the road and check your rearview mirrors every 2–5 seconds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it acceptable to drive on the shoulder to pass another car?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If the shoulder is wide enough.
note: Never pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder; it is unsafe and illegal in most situations.

question: What should you expect about traction when driving on gravel or dirt roads?
options: a:Your tires have less traction than on pavement so you must slow down,b:Visibility is better on gravel and dirt roads,c:Your tires grip the road better than on pavement,d:You can stop more quickly on dirt surfaces
note: Loose gravel and dirt reduce traction and increase stopping distance. Reduce speed and avoid sudden maneuvers on such surfaces.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light without stopping, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the light turns green.,b:Follow the officer's direction and go through without stopping.,c:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,d:Ignore the officer and obey the signal.
note: An officer's traffic directions override traffic signals; follow their instructions.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always:
options: a:Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.,b:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,c:Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.
note: Scan to the left and right at places where people or other vehicles may enter your path to ensure safety.

question: When driving on snow or ice, which practice helps prevent skidding on steep downgrades?
options: a:Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.,b:Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.,c:Maintain a close following distance to the vehicle ahead.
note: Use a low gear to control speed on steep, slippery declines; keep extra following distance and avoid sudden stops.

question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:
options: a:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.,b:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,c:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots; avoid traveling alongside them for extended periods so the driver can see you.

question: What is the best way to reduce the risk of hydroplaning in wet conditions?
options: a:Slow down and drive at a reduced speed for the conditions.,b:Drive at a speed appropriate for ideal conditions.,c:Apply the brakes as soon as the car begins to skid.
note: Reduce speed in rain to give tires time to channel water and maintain contact with the road.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.,c:Only if you are stopped and cited.
note: You must present proof of financial responsibility (insurance) to an officer after a traffic stop or collision when requested.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights and siren, you must:
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until the vehicle has passed.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until the vehicle has passed.,c:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed.
note: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass safely.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line indicates that passing is:
options: a:Permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,b:Not permitted from either direction.,c:Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.
note: Traffic beside the broken line may pass when safe; traffic beside the solid line may not pass.

question: After passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After about three seconds.,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,d:When the other driver signals you to return.
note: Move back when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror; always signal before changing lanes.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.,b:If you are under the legal blood alcohol concentration limit, your driving isn't impaired.,c:Alcohol affects judgement, which is needed to drive safely.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment even at low levels; safe driving requires clear judgement and coordination.

question: If you see heavy smoke covering the roadway ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your four-way flashers and continue.,b:Reduce your speed, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway.,c:Turn on your high beam headlights and continue.
note: Slow down, pull off the road to the right, and stop until you can safely continue; smoke can be hazardous to breathe.

question: Because motorcycles and mopeds are harder to see, what should motorists do?
options: a:Share the lane with them.,b:Make frequent visual checks and be alert.,c:Drive faster to pass them quickly.,d:Ignore small vehicles in traffic.
note: Motorcycles can be hidden in blind spots; drivers should make constant visual checks and stay alert.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what conditions may you proceed on a red light when a green arrow is also displayed?
options: a:If you are in the proper lane and the way is clear.,b:Only after coming to a full stop.,c:Only after the arrow turns off.,d:Never; red overrides the arrow.
note: A green arrow allows movement in the arrow's direction when you are in the corresponding lane and the way is clear.

question: If you approach a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop well behind the gates and wait until they lift and the tracks are clear.,b:Slow down and proceed if you think no train is coming.,c:Drive around the gates if you cannot see a train.
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to go around lowered gates; always stop and wait until it is safe to proceed.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Driving aggressively to assert the right-of-way.,b:Using safe strategies to prevent crashes.,c:Driving more dangerously than other drivers.
note: Defensive driving means adjusting to conditions, staying aware of others, and using safe tactics to avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,b:Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.,c:Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.
note: Pass promptly and safely to reduce the time you are in the opposing lane or in a blind spot, and return when it is safe.

question: What is the definition of distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: Distracted driving is any activity that diverts your eyes, hands, or mind from driving and increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic before merging?
options: a:Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to check blind spots, then merge when safe.,b:Use only your rearview mirror.,c:Use rearview and side mirrors but do not look over your shoulder.
note: Combine mirror checks with a quick shoulder glance to confirm the travel lane is clear before merging.

question: What does a curb painted red indicate?
options: a:Loading zone.,b:No parking, standing, or stopping.,c:Passenger pick-up/drop-off only.,d:Emergency parking only.
note: A red-painted curb means no stopping, standing, or parking is permitted.

question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:The same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.,b:The same as a yield sign.,c:The light is about to turn green.
note: A flashing red signal requires a complete stop and yielding to other traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

question: If your wheels run off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do first?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes,b:Turn the front wheels sharply to re-enter the pavement,c:Apply full brakes immediately and stop,d:Accelerate and then steer back onto the pavement
note: Slow down gradually while holding the wheel steady, check traffic, and return to the roadway when safe; do not jerk the wheel back onto pavement.

question: A driver's license is considered which of the following?
options: a:A privilege, not a right.,b:A right, not a privilege.,c:A requirement.
note: Driving is a privilege granted under law and can be suspended or revoked for violations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, how fast should you be driving?
options: a:At or near the speed of freeway traffic.,b:Much slower than the freeway traffic.,c:At a speed significantly above the posted limit.,d:At any comfortable speed.
