note: Merge at or near the speed of traffic on the freeway so you can safely blend into traffic flow.

question: What is the only thing that will lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drinking coffee,b:Time,c:Taking a cold shower,d:Eating fatty foods
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and eliminate alcohol. Nothing else reliably speeds up the process.

question: What is the correct response to a tire blowout while driving?
options: a:Tap or pump the brakes rapidly.,b:Slow down gradually and apply the brakes lightly.,c:Brake hard immediately and steer to shoulder.
note: If a tire blows out, ease off the accelerator, hold the wheel firmly, slow down gradually and apply brakes lightly once the vehicle has slowed.

question: Which ability is affected first by alcohol?
options: a:Judgment,b:Vision,c:Balance
note: Alcohol first impairs judgment and decision-making, which affects all other driving skills.

question: If someone is following you too closely on a two-lane road and you cannot change lanes, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.,b:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.,c:Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.
note: If you cannot safely change lanes, gently slow to encourage the tailgater to pass; avoid sudden braking.

question: If the roadway ahead is flooded, what should you do?
options: a:Turn around and seek an alternate route — do not attempt to drive through the water.,b:Slam on the brakes to avoid the water.,c:Drive only in the center of the roadway across the flooded area.
note: Never drive through floodwater; depth and road damage can be deceptive and very dangerous.

question: What must drivers do when a school bus is loading or unloading children?
options: a:Stop completely, regardless of your direction of travel.,b:Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction as the bus.,c:Slow down and be ready to stop.
note: You must come to a complete stop for a bus with extended stop arm and flashing red lights, from either direction.

question: If dust or smoke reduces your ability to see other vehicles, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on parking lights and continue at normal speed.,b:Turn on emergency flashers only.,c:Slow down and turn on your headlights.
note: Turn on headlights any time visibility is reduced so others can see you, and reduce speed to match conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or passing, what should you do?
options: a:Signal and check mirrors and blind spots.,b:Assume other drivers will make space for you.,c:Only check your inside rearview mirror.
note: Signal every lane change, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check blind spots before moving laterally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you treat an intersection where the traffic signal is not working?
options: a:Treat it as an all-way stop: come to a complete stop and yield before entering.,b:Proceed without stopping if the intersection looks clear.,c:Drive through quickly to avoid delaying traffic.,d:Follow the vehicle ahead without stopping.
note: When signals are out, stop as you would at a stop sign and yield the right-of-way before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue driving without stopping.
note: When two vehicles arrive together at a four-way stop, yield to the driver on your right.

question: When a stopped school bus ahead of you on your side of the road has red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Slow to 10 mph and pass cautiously.,b:Stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing.,c:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,d:Proceed if no children are visible.
note: You must stop for a stopped school bus on your side with red lights flashing and may not proceed until the lights are off.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, what should you do immediately?
options: a:Find a safe place to stop and take a break or nap.,b:Try to fight it and continue driving.,c:Take caffeine pills and keep driving.
note: Drowsiness reduces attention and reaction time—stop safely and rest or change drivers when necessary.

question: What should you do when you see a deep puddle on the roadway?
options: a:Maintain posted speed to get through it.,b:Avoid the puddle if possible.,c:Shift into neutral while crossing.,d:Brake hard just before entering.
note: Avoid deep puddles to reduce the risk of hydroplaning or vehicle damage.

question: Before switching on the ignition, you should:
options: a:Buckle your safety belt.,b:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,c:Both of the above.
note: Develop the habit of fastening your seat belt and ensuring passengers are belted before starting the vehicle.

question: When parking on a hill, what is the correct action to take?
options: a:Turn a rear wheel so it touches the curb,b:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park,c:Leave the transmission in neutral and set the parking brake,d:With no curb, point the front wheels parallel to the road
note: Always leave the vehicle in gear or in park and set the parking brake. Turn the wheels toward or away from the curb as appropriate so the vehicle will not roll into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is NOT a safe practice on an interstate highway?
options: a:Change lanes without signaling.,b:Slower traffic must keep to the right.,c:If you miss your exit, you must go to the next exit.
note: You should always signal before changing lanes. Do not back up or make U-turns on interstates; proceed to the next exit if you miss yours.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Signal before changing lanes,b:Never attempt to pass or otherwise change lanes in an intersection,c:Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder,d:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane
note: Never pass or change lanes within an intersection. Always check mirrors, blind spots, and signal before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must drivers turning left yield to?
options: a:Overtaking cars.,b:Oncoming cars going straight.,c:No one — they have the right-of-way.,d:Cars behind them.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles that are going straight through the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before stopping at a traffic signal or sign, what should you check?
options: a:Press down hard on the accelerator.,b:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,c:Set the parking brake.
note: Check mirrors for traffic behind and around you as you slow so you can stop smoothly and safely.

question: What must vehicles do at a crosswalk?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians who have the right-of-way.,b:Expect pedestrians to yield to vehicles.,c:Require construction workers to yield to vehicular traffic.
note: Pedestrians in a crosswalk have the right-of-way; drivers must stop for them unless traffic signals indicate otherwise.

question: What is the best way to check a blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder into the blind spot.,b:Use your side mirror only.,c:Rely on the inside rearview mirror only.
note: Even with proper mirror adjustment, always glance over your shoulder to inspect blind spots before changing lanes.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection require you to do?
options: a:Stop completely and wait four seconds.,b:Yield to all traffic before entering.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution, yielding as necessary to other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Cutting the corner short and interfering with other traffic.,b:Slowing down as you approach the turn.,c:Using your turn signal to alert others.
note: Do not cut the corner when turning left; signal and slow in advance so the turn is completed safely.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal indicate for drivers preparing to turn?
options: a:You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.,b:You should speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.,c:You should prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.
note: A solid yellow arrow warns that the green arrow protection is ending; you should prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

question: With oncoming traffic to your left and parked cars to your right, how should you steer?
options: a:Steer a middle course between the oncoming vehicles and parked cars.,b:Stay as close to parked vehicles as possible.,c:Move closer to oncoming traffic to give parked vehicles room.
note: Position your vehicle roughly in the center of the available lane to avoid hazards on both sides.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection at the posted speed when the light turns yellow, you should:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Ignore the signal and proceed normally.,d:Honk and proceed.
note: If you can stop safely when a light turns yellow, do so; otherwise proceed cautiously through the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does safe interstate driving require?
options: a:The ability to safely drive at increased speeds and constant alertness.,b:Only knowing where exits are.,c:Constantly using cruise control.,d:Only being able to drive at the posted speed limit.
note: Interstate driving requires being alert and able to operate safely at higher speeds when appropriate.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips along road edges or centerlines?
options: a:To alert inattentive drivers through vibration and sound.,b:To test vehicle tire condition.,c:To mark pedestrian crossings.,d:To slow traffic like speed bumps.
note: Rumble strips create noise and vibration to warn drivers they are leaving the travel lane or approaching a hazard.

question: Which statement about driving through roadwork zones is true?
options: a:Fines are the same as in normal traffic.,b:You must slow down for the Cone Zone.,c:Slow only if workers are visible.
note: You should slow down through work zones; many states emphasize slowing for the Cone Zone to protect workers and drivers.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, you should:
options: a:Speed up to scare them away.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Quickly swerve into the next lane.
note: Animals can move unpredictably; reduce speed and proceed carefully when they are near the road.

question: Which factor affects how quickly alcohol is absorbed by a person?
options: a:Weight,b:Height,c:Intelligence
note: Absorption varies with weight, sex, food in the stomach, and the amount consumed, among other factors.

question: How do stopping distance and severity of collisions change with vehicle speed?
options: a:They decrease as speed increases.,b:They are unaffected by speed.,c:They increase as speed increases.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and the force of impact, raising the likelihood and severity of crashes.

question: At what speed can a car begin to hydroplane in standing water?
options: a:35 miles per hour,b:45 miles per hour,c:40 miles per hour
note: Hydroplaning can start at relatively low highway speeds (around 35 mph) when there is standing water.

question: How are bicycles treated when used on roadways?
options: a:As vehicles subject to the same rules.,b:As hazards that must be avoided at all costs.,c:As pedestrians.,d:As vehicles that always have the right-of-way.
note: Bicycles are considered vehicles on roadways and riders must follow the same rules as motor vehicles.

question: How should you respond at an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Come to a full stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and remain stopped while the light is red regardless of conditions.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: stop, yield, and go when the way is clear.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded.,b:Toward the center of the roadway.,c:Straight ahead in your lane.
note: Look toward the right edge of the road and use peripheral vision to follow the vehicle’s position until it passes.

question: Which statement about medications and driving is true?
options: a:Even over-the-counter medicines can impair your driving.,b:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,c:All prescription drugs are safe if you don't feel drowsy.
note: Legal prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair judgment, coordination, and reaction time; always know a drug’s effects.

question: When driving at night, what should you remember?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Increase following distance at night for extra stopping time; use high beams only when appropriate and avoid glare from oncoming vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles,b:Wherever signs and/or pavement markings permit passing,c:Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles
note: Pass only where signs and pavement markings allow and when you have sufficient space and visibility to do so safely.

question: When driving at night you should:
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Increase following distance at night to allow more time to react; use high beams appropriately and avoid staring at oncoming lights.

question: When are headlights required by Mississippi law?
options: a:Between sunset and sunrise.,b:When the temperature drops below freezing.,c:When you are tired.,d:Only during snowstorms.
note: Mississippi law requires headlights between sunset and sunrise; use low beams within 500 feet of other vehicles.

question: Consistently looking far ahead while driving on the highway helps to:
options: a:Helps you keep up with traffic.,b:Reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning.,c:Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.
note: Scanning far ahead enables smoother driving, fewer sudden maneuvers, and better reaction time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about changing lanes is correct?
options: a:You only need to look over your shoulder for left lane changes.,b:Look over the shoulder corresponding to the direction of the lane change to check blind spots.,c:If you have two outside mirrors, you have no blind spots.
note: Signal, check mirrors, and look over the left or right shoulder as appropriate to check blind spots before changing lanes.

question: If a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you creating a hazard, what should you do first?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal,b:Honk and apply the brakes firmly,c:Swerve into the lane next to you,d:Speed up to pass the vehicle
note: Remove your foot from the accelerator to increase space between you and the other vehicle; avoid sudden braking or swerving unless necessary.

question: If your vehicle becomes disabled on a highway, where should you park if possible?
options: a:In the rightmost travel lane.,b:With all four wheels off the main-traveled portion of the highway.,c:Where you stopped and leave the hazard lights off.,d:Facing oncoming traffic.
note: If your car is disabled, park with all wheels off the main-traveled roadway when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is green but a police officer signals for you to stop, you should:
options: a:Obey the officer.,b:Obey the traffic signal.,c:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.
note: Follow directions from law enforcement even if they conflict with traffic signals or signs.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you in a city street, what must you do?
options: a:Stay in lane and slow down.,b:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,c:Drive to the right edge and slow down but remain moving.,d:Ignore it and keep driving.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping until they pass; if in an intersection, clear it first then stop.

question: If the rear of your vehicle begins to skid left, how should you steer?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel to the left (in the direction of the skid) to correct it.,b:Turn the steering wheel to the right to counter the skid.,c:Do not turn the steering wheel at all.
note: Steer into the direction of the skid to help the vehicle regain traction (unless ABS/braking procedure differs).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection where the traffic light is also working, whose directions should you follow?
options: a:The directions of the traffic light.,b:The officer's directions.,c:Ignore both and proceed cautiously.
note: A police officer's signals take precedence over traffic control devices, so follow the officer's directions when present.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, which of the following is true?
options: a:They may use the left lane.,b:They may wait on the side of the road.,c:They may cut through all lanes.
note: Bicyclists may take the left lane when preparing to make a left turn; expect bicyclists to behave like other vehicles in such situations.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean for passing?
options: a:No passing is allowed from either direction.,b:Passing allowed from both directions.,c:Passing allowed only from your direction.,d:Passing allowed at certain times of day.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate opposing traffic and prohibit passing from either direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to exit the interstate, when should you reduce your speed?
options: a:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,b:As you approach the deceleration lane.,c:Immediately after entering the deceleration lane.
note: Maintain highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane, then slow to the advisory speed posted for the exit ramp.

question: What is the only reliable way to lower your blood alcohol concentration?
options: a:Give your body time to metabolize the alcohol.,b:Drink strong coffee to sober up quickly.,c:Take a cold shower to become alert.
note: Only time will reduce BAC; coffee, showers, or exercise do not speed alcohol elimination.

question: When you approach a flashing red traffic light, you must:
options: a:Are traveling in the wrong direction.,b:Treat the intersection as if it is controlled by a stop sign.,c:May not proceed until it changes to green.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop; proceed only when it is safe, just like a stop sign.

question: Which statement about driving and medications is accurate?
options: a:Many cold medicines and other over-the-counter drugs can cause drowsiness and impair driving.,b:Over-the-counter medicines cannot impair driving if taken as directed.,c:If a doctor prescribes a medication, it is always safe to drive while using it.
note: Many common medications can affect alertness and coordination; check labels and know how they affect you before driving.

question: What does a solid yellow line beside a broken yellow line indicate?
options: a:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass when safe; vehicles next to the solid line may not.,b:Traffic in both directions may pass freely.,c:Only the lane next to the solid line may pass.
note: When your side has the broken line you may pass if it is safe; the solid-line side may not pass.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a:Three,b:Two,c:One
note: Even a single drink can impair judgement, reaction time, and driving ability.

question: When passing a row of parked cars, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:Someone or something unexpectedly entering your lane.,b:All pedestrians to wait for you.,c:To drive very close to the parked cars to allow traffic flow.,d:Parked cars to always stay put.
note: People or vehicles may step out from between parked cars, so leave space and be prepared to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to make a left turn on a red light after stopping?
options: a:Only when you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street,b:When traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street,c:Whenever you yield to all other traffic,d:Only if there is a posted sign allowing it
note: After a complete stop, a left turn on red is permitted only when you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street, and only if no sign prohibits it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you approach a roundabout, you should slow down and do what?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians only.,b:Yield to vehicles already in the roundabout only.,c:Yield to both pedestrians and vehicles already in the roundabout.
note: When entering a roundabout you must yield to pedestrians and bicyclists and to traffic already circulating in the roundabout.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline on your side of the road mean?
options: a:You may cross the line to pass when it is safe to do so.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:A construction zone is ahead.
note: A broken yellow beside your lane indicates you may pass if the way ahead is clear and it is safe.

question: A driver's license is considered what under the law?
options: a:A mandatory requirement.,b:A privilege granted by the state.,c:A constitutional right.
note: Driving is a privilege granted by the state that can be revoked or suspended for unsafe or illegal behavior.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When moving into a gap in highway traffic, what should you do first?
options: a:Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead to judge the gap.,b:Speed up and force other vehicles to make room.,c:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
note: Before merging or changing lanes, check mirrors and blind spots, then time your entry to a safe gap.

question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a two-lane road and keep passing, what is the likely result?
options: a:Get you to your destination much more quickly and safely,b:Increase your chances of a collision,c:Help prevent traffic congestion,d:Improve fuel efficiency
note: Continuously passing on two-lane roads increases your exposure to hazards and raises the chance of a crash.

question: When changing lanes, what is the correct way to check the area you cannot see with mirrors?
options: a:Look over your shoulder toward the direction you plan to move.,b:Rely only on the rearview mirror.,c:Use only the left side mirror.
note: Check blind spots by glancing over your shoulder; mirrors alone may not reveal vehicles in those areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstances may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:Under no circumstances — you must not block an intersection.,b:If you entered the intersection on a green light.,c:Only during rush hour traffic.
note: Do not enter unless you can clear the intersection; blocking an intersection can lead to citations and crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn from a multi-lane one-way street onto another one-way street?
options: a:The lane closest to the left curb.,b:Any lane as long as it appears safe.,c:The center lane of the road.
note: When turning left from a one-way to a one-way, start from the far-left lane and end in the leftmost lane available.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in the left lane and vehicles are passing you on the right, what should you do when a driver behind wants to go faster?
options: a:Stay in your lane so you don't impede traffic,b:Drive onto the left shoulder to let others pass,c:Move into the right lane when it is safe,d:Speed up to maintain the left lane
note: Use the left lane for passing and turning. If you are driving more slowly than surrounding traffic, safely move into the right lane to allow faster vehicles to pass.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, what is the safest choice?
options: a:Find a safe place to park and take a short nap or rest.,b:Increase your speed to get to your destination sooner.,c:Turn up the radio volume to stay awake.
note: If you experience drowsiness, stop safely and rest; fighting fatigue while driving is hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?
options: a:No — driving too slowly can block traffic and create hazards.,b:Yes — it is always a good defensive technique.,c:Yes — it is always safer than driving faster.
note: Drive at a safe speed for conditions; going excessively slower than traffic can be dangerous and lead to citations.

question: Which is a dangerous habit when driving through work zones?
options: a:Tailgating another vehicle.,b:Failing to watch for workers and equipment.,c:Both tailgating and failing to watch for workers are dangerous.
note: Tailgating and inattention to workers or equipment in a work zone greatly increase the risk of collisions and injuries.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another car, how can you tell you have enough space to return to your lane?
options: a:You can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.,b:The other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.,c:You look over your shoulder and see the passed car's right side.,d:You are one car length ahead.
note: You may move back into the lane once you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: If you park uphill on a two-way street with no curb, which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Turn them toward the center of the road.,b:Turn them away from the center of the road (toward the side).,c:Keep them straight ahead.,d:Turn them toward oncoming traffic.
note: On hills without a curb, turn wheels so the vehicle would roll away from the center of the road if brakes fail.

question: Why is driving at night generally more hazardous than daytime driving?
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night.
note: Reduced visibility and glare at night limit how far and how well you can see ahead; use headlights and drive cautiously.

question: Why is extra space needed in front of a large truck?
options: a:To let other drivers merge ahead of the truck.,b:Because trucks need more distance to stop.,c:To allow trucks to speed up.,d:Because truck pilots require a buffer for turns.
note: Trucks require longer stopping distances than cars; do not cut in front of trucks and then slow down.

question: When are streets and highways most slippery?
options: a:After it has been raining heavily for hours.,b:When the road is completely dry.,c:Just after it begins to rain.
note: Road surfaces can be extremely slippery shortly after rain begins because water mixes with oil and residues on the pavement.

question: On a green arrow signal, what must you do before turning?
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian still in the intersection.,b:Wait a full four seconds before moving.,c:Proceed without yielding because you have a protected turn.
note: A green arrow gives permission to turn, but you must first yield to any vehicle or pedestrian still in the intersection.

question: A large truck turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction:
options: a:Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.,b:May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.,c:May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
note: Long trucks often swing wide on right turns because their rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels.

question: Why should you increase following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:To better see around the sides of the vehicle and to avoid being in its blind spots.,b:Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before trying to pass them.,c:To get caught in the vehicle's slipstream for better fuel efficiency.
note: Large vehicles can obstruct your view of the road ahead and may have large blind spots; leave extra space for safety.

question: How does stopping distance and crash severity change as speed increases?
options: a:Stopping distance and severity increase as speed increases.,b:They decrease as speed increases.,c:They are unaffected by speed.,d:Stopping distance increases but severity decreases.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and make collisions more severe.

question: What behavior blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,b:Slowing down to look at a collision or unusual incident.,c:Using public transportation.,d:Keeping a steady speed.
note: Rubbernecking — slowing to look at crashes — contributes to congestion and should be avoided.

question: To improve visibility reduced by rain or fog, drivers should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Use low beams in rain, fog, or snow because high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: On roads where traffic is moving 50–55 mph, how is your accident risk minimized?
options: a:By driving a few mph faster than most traffic.,b:By traveling within the flow of traffic.,c:By driving much slower than the flow.,d:By constantly changing speeds to match others.
note: Adjust speed to travel smoothly with other traffic (within posted limits); similar speeds reduce collision risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn from a one-way street, which lane must you be in?
options: a:The lane nearest the left curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the right curb.
note: Turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to go; for left turns on one-way streets use the far-left lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your original lane after passing a vehicle, what should you confirm?
options: a:That the passed vehicle honks to allow you back.,b:That you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:That you flash your headlights as a signal.
note: Only move back into the lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating a safe gap.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, what is permitted?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the left.,b:Passing is permitted from the right.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow center lines mean no passing from either direction because traffic moves in opposite directions.

question: From which vehicle areas should you remove snow, frost, and ice before driving?
options: a:Just the windshield.,b:All windows and mirrors.,c:Only the windshield and passenger window.
note: You must clear snow, ice, and frost from all windows and mirrors so you have full visibility before driving.

question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?
options: a:Follow the driver ahead closely.,b:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.,c:Pass other vehicles whenever possible.
note: In work zones increase your following distance, avoid tailgating, and obey signs to protect workers and other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian began crossing after the Dont Walk signal and is in the roadway when your light turns green. What should you do?
options: a:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Wait until the pedestrian has crossed before going.
note: Vehicles must yield to pedestrians already in the intersection; wait until they finish crossing before proceeding even when your light turns green.

question: What is one effective way to reduce incidents of road rage?
options: a:Always signal when changing lanes.,b:Use your horn frequently to warn others.,c:Talk on your cell phone to calm down.
note: Signal your intentions and follow traffic laws to reduce misunderstandings and help prevent road rage incidents.

question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Use your high beam headlights,b:Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.,c:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.
note: Use low beams when following another vehicle to avoid blinding the driver ahead; save high beams for dark, empty roads.

question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing in the middle of the street, what must you do?
options: a:You must stop and yield to them.,b:You do not have to stop for them.,c:Honk to make them move out of the way.
note: Even if pedestrians are crossing illegally, drivers must still yield and stop to avoid hitting them.

question: If weather conditions are poor, what should drivers do with speed?
options: a:Decrease their speed.,b:Increase their speed.,c:Maintain normal speed.,d:Turn on cruise control.
note: Reduce speed in poor weather to maintain control and account for longer stopping distances.

question: If a stopped school bus in your lane has red lights flashing, what action is required?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped while the red lights flash.,b:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.,c:Stop only if children are visible.,d:Proceed if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.
note: Stop and remain stopped for a school bus with flashing red lights unless the roadway is divided and you are on the opposite side.

question: At dawn, dusk, or during rain or snow when visibility is low, a good way to make your vehicle more visible is to turn on:
options: a:Your parking lights.,b:Up the instrumental panel lights.,c:Your headlights.
note: Use your headlights (low beams) when visibility is reduced to help others see your vehicle.

question: How should you adjust speed on a narrow, winding road?
options: a:Increase your speed to clear the curve quickly.,b:Decrease your speed to match conditions.,c:Maintain the normal posted speed at all times.
note: Reduce your speed on winding or hazardous roads; posted limits assume ideal conditions.

question: Vehicles stopped behind a school bus with red lights flashing must remain stopped until:
options: a:All students are off the bus.,b:The stop arm is retracted.,c:The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.
note: Drivers must remain stopped until the bus turns off its flashing red lights, retracts the stop arm, and begins moving.

question: If a pedestrian is crossing your lane where there is no marked crosswalk, what must you do?
options: a:Cautiously drive around them.,b:Make sure they see you before proceeding.,c:Stop and allow the pedestrian to finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if there is no marked crosswalk; stop and let them finish crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, besides checking mirrors, what else should you do?
options: a:Glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.,b:Never look over your right shoulder.,c:Always slow down dramatically.,d:Assume nothing is there.
note: Check mirrors and glance over your shoulder to ensure the blind spot is clear before changing lanes.

question: How can you help drivers behind you maintain a safe following distance?
options: a:By maintaining a steady speed.,b:By driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,c:By braking unexpectedly.,d:By frequently changing lanes.
note: Maintaining a steady speed and signaling in advance helps the driver behind you keep a safe distance.

question: When a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you expect?
options: a:The child will always follow traffic laws.,b:The child may act unpredictably; expect the unexpected.,c:The child will yield to your vehicle.,d:You should beep to make them move.
note: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable; drivers should be cautious and expect sudden moves.

question: When following a motorcycle, what should you do about following distance?
options: a:Allow a larger following distance (3–4 seconds).,b:Drive more slowly than the motorcycle.,c:Be ready to use your horn constantly.,d:Tailgate to prevent lane changes.
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly and are less stable; allow a larger following distance of 3–4 seconds.

question: Which of the following commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Scanning the environment and staying focused,b:Exceeding the posted speed limit and driving too fast for conditions,c:Getting adequate rest and staying alert,d:Using signals when changing lanes
note: Driving above the speed limit or too fast for conditions increases crash risk. Being alert and scanning reduces risk.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Drive at the posted speed.,c:Speed up.
note: Slow down when road surfaces are wet, snowy, or icy because traction is reduced.

question: If your tires seem to lift off the road surface, what should you do first?
options: a:Ease your foot off the gas pedal and avoid braking.,b:Pump the brakes quickly and firmly to slow down.,c:Shift into a lower gear to reduce speed.
note: If your tires lose contact with the road, lift off the accelerator and do not brake or steer until traction returns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To avoid traffic merging from on-ramps to your right on an interstate, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Change lanes to the left when safe.,b:Slow down drastically.,c:Stay in your lane and maintain position.
note: When traffic permits, move out of the right lane to the left to allow entering vehicles room to merge safely.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Drive faster than the train to beat it.,b:Look for a way around any lowered gates.,c:Be prepared to stop if a train is approaching.
note: Railroad crossings require caution; be prepared to stop and never go around lowered gates or barriers.

question: Which of these statements about blind spots is accurate?
options: a:They disappear if you have outside mirrors on both sides.,b:Large trucks have larger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be fully checked with mirrors only.,d:Blind spots are only present at high speeds.
note: Blind spots are areas mirrors don't show; large trucks have larger blind spots than most cars.

question: Which statement about large trucks is true?
options: a:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.,c:They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.
note: Due to their size and weight, large trucks require much more distance to stop than passenger cars.

question: To help prevent skids on slippery surfaces, you should:
options: a:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,b:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.,c:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
note: Reduce speed before curves and intersections; braking while turning can cause skids.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate about passing?
options: a:Passing on the left is allowed when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is prohibited.,c:Passing on the right is allowed.,d:Both directions may pass freely.
note: A broken yellow centerline means you may cross to pass on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, when may you turn left onto another one-way street?
options: a:Only if you accelerate before the turn.,b:If traffic on the street you are turning onto moves to the right.,c:If traffic on that street is moving to the left and no sign prohibits the turn.
note: You may turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves left, provided no signs prohibit the turn and you turn into the proper lane.

question: If a vehicle is equipped with airbags, what should you still do?
options: a:Always wear both lap and shoulder seat belts.,b:Rely on airbags and forgo seat belts.,c:Wear only the lap belt.
note: Airbags provide supplemental protection but lap and shoulder belts must still be worn for maximum safety.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered distracted driving?
options: a:It occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.,b:It causes the driver to be concerned about the cost of the call.,c:It is an activity that draws the attention of other drivers.
note: Cell phones take your eyes, hands, and mental focus away from driving, increasing crash risk.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing.,b:You must stop when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.,c:You should always speed up to cross faster.,d:Never expect trains to be present at crossings.
note: You must stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what speed should you aim for?
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway so you can merge smoothly.,b:Five to ten mph slower than the freeway traffic.,c:The posted speed limit for unrelated freeway traffic regardless of flow.
note: Enter at a speed close to the main traffic flow to merge safely without disrupting other drivers.

question: What should you do to check a vehicle's blind spots?
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction of the blind spot.,b:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.,c:Use the outside mirror only.,d:Assume mirrors show the blind spot.
note: To see blind spots, glance over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move before changing lanes.

question: Backing your vehicle is:
options: a:Always dangerous.,b:Dangerous if you have a helper.,c:Only dangerous in large vehicles.
note: Backing is inherently risky because rear visibility is limited; use caution and helpers if necessary.

question: Where should a driver watch while operating the vehicle?
options: a:Only directly in front of the car.,b:Only at the center of the road ahead.,c:To the sides, ahead, and behind the vehicle.
note: Good drivers continuously scan beside, ahead, and to the rear to be aware of changing conditions around the vehicle.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what must you do?
options: a:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead and slow down.,b:Change lanes and keep your speed steady.,c:Speed up to clear the area.,d:Ignore the signs if no workers are visible.
note: Construction zones may have workers and lane changes; slow down and be prepared to stop.

question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow signal, how must you proceed?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Maintain your normal speed.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow and proceed with care after checking for hazards.

question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb.,b:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,c:Only when pulling next to the curb.,d:Never; signals are unnecessary in parking.
note: Signal both when pulling toward the curb and when pulling away so others know your intentions.

question: To make quick, safe turns you should place your hands:
options: a:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.,b:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.,c:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
note: Place both hands on opposite sides of the wheel (about 9 and 3 o'clock) for better control during turns.

question: What should you do when taking any medication and planning to drive?
options: a:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about how it may affect driving.,b:Open your window and drive faster.,c:Have someone follow you home.,d:Drive only during daylight.
note: Both prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair driving; consult a healthcare professional about effects.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you're driving, what is the correct immediate response?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly and steer quickly to the right.,b:Use the brakes lightly and slow down gradually.,c:Pump the brakes repeatedly.
note: For a sudden blowout, keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and use the brakes lightly once the vehicle has slowed.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of drug?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:An antihistamine.,c:A depressant.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant that impairs judgment, coordination, and reaction times.

question: Who must drivers obey at construction sites giving traffic instructions?
options: a:Security guards in parking lots.,b:Flaggers (signal persons) directing traffic.,c:Other drivers whose vehicles are disabled.,d:Construction workers only.
note: Drivers are required to obey instructions from flaggers to protect workers and road users.

question: Why is night driving more hazardous than daytime driving?
options: a:The speed limit is increased at night.,b:There are fewer cars on the road at night.,c:Distance and speed of other vehicles are harder to judge in the dark.
note: Reduced visibility at night limits how far you can see and makes it harder to judge the distance and speed of other vehicles.

question: Why should you avoid using high beams in fog or mist?
options: a:The light will reflect back into your eyes, reducing visibility.,b:Approaching vehicles might not see you.,c:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.
note: High beams reflect off fog, causing glare and making it harder to see; use low beams or fog lights instead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,b:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,c:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.
note: When parked on a slope, turn your wheels toward or away from the curb/edge as appropriate to prevent rolling into traffic.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do about braking?
options: a:Brake lightly to regain control.,b:Stay off the brakes and steer to control the vehicle.,c:Brake abruptly to stop the skid.
note: Do not use the brakes during a skid; instead, steer in the direction needed to regain control and let the vehicle slow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Return to the lane only after you can see the entire passed vehicle in your mirror and you have checked blind spots.

question: How close to another vehicle must you be to switch from high beams to low beams?
options: a:Within 1,000 feet.,b:Within 500 feet.,c:Within 200 feet.,d:Within 50 feet.
note: You must use low beams when within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or when following within 500 feet of another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You plan to make a left turn at the next corner. To whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Only to vehicles turning left as well.,b:All approaching vehicles and pedestrians with the right-of-way.,c:Only to pedestrians waiting at the curb.
note: When turning left you must yield to all oncoming vehicles and pedestrians who have the right-of-way before completing the turn.

question: If your vehicle has an anti-lock braking system and you must stop on snow or ice, what should you do?
options: a:Pump the brakes manually.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Stay off the brakes and let the vehicle roll to a stop.
note: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly; the system will pulse the brakes to help maintain steering control during hard braking.

question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:
options: a:The vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.,b:The yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.,c:The yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.
note: If the center line next to your lane is broken, you may pass when it is safe to do so; a solid line on your side prohibits passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When multiple vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled intersection, who goes first?
options: a:Yield to the vehicle on your right.,b:Yield to the vehicle on your left.,c:Wait until the intersection is empty.,d:The largest vehicle goes first.
note: If vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
note: If the broken line is on your side, you may pass when safe; if the solid line is on your side, passing is prohibited.

question: At a school crossing sign, you should:
options: a:Always stop, whether there is a stop sign or not.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: School crossing signs warn of children; slow down and be prepared to stop when you see them.

question: If a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is waiting to cross at a corner, what must you do before turning?
options: a:Wait until the person has crossed the street and is clear of your path.,b:Tell the pedestrian when it is safe to cross.,c:Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
note: Pedestrians who are blind or visually impaired must be given the right-of-way; wait until they are safely across.

question: When is highway pavement especially slippery and treacherous?
options: a:Just after rain begins, when oil and dirt combine with water to form a greasy film.,b:After it has been raining for several hours.,c:One to two hours into a rainstorm.
note: Roads are most slippery at the start of rainfall due to accumulated oils mixing with the water; slow down accordingly.

question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted when safe.,b:Both lanes are going the same direction.,c:Passing is prohibited.,d:The lane ends ahead.
note: Dashed yellow lines separate opposing-direction lanes and mean passing is allowed when safe.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,b:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a complete stop, check the traffic, and go when it is safe to do so.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign: stop fully, yield, and proceed only when safe.

question: For drivers 21 and older it is illegal to drive with a BAC of:
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: Mississippi law prohibits driving with a BAC of 0.08% or higher for drivers 21 and older.

question: Which of these slows reaction time and impairs driving ability?
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Working hard.,c:Sleeping well.
note: Alcohol reduces reflexes, impairs judgment, and degrades vision and coordination, increasing crash risk even at low levels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is blocking an intersection when your light turns green, what should you do?
options: a:Partially enter to assert right-of-way.,b:Wait outside the intersection until you can clear it completely.,c:Enter and wait in the intersection until traffic clears.,d:Honk to clear traffic.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can get completely through it; blocking an intersection can result in a citation.

question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrian waves you on.,b:Only if the pedestrian is using a phone.,c:At all times when they are in the crosswalk.
note: Drivers must stop for and yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk; proceed only when the crosswalk is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Check side mirrors and look over your shoulder to ensure the lane is clear.,b:Only check the inside rearview mirror.,c:Slow down significantly before moving.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors, signal, and look over your shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear.

question: When a school bus has its stop arm out and red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the bus retracts the arm and the lights turn off.,b:Sound your horn before passing on the left.,c:Proceed if you think most children are finished exiting.
note: Always stop for a school bus with the stop arm extended and flashing red lights to protect boarding/exiting children.

question: How should you behave when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Stop to watch workers.,b:Slow down and avoid slowing to stare at the scene.,c:Decrease your following distance.,d:Pass quickly without regard to signs.
note: Do not rubberneck; pass carefully and maintain safe following distance to avoid causing congestion.

question: What are 'no zones' around large trucks?
options: a:Are areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are so close that they restrict the truck driver's ability to stop and maneuver safely,b:Provide several car lengths of safe following distance behind a truck,c:Are places where it is safest for cars to pass a truck,d:Are areas where trucks must yield to cars
note: No zones are large blind spots around trucks and buses. Being in a no zone means the truck driver may not see you and your presence can limit the truck's ability to stop or maneuver.

question: If you see pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Continue ahead; the motorist has the right-of-way.,b:Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.,c:Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.
note: You must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk and wait until they have crossed before proceeding.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes hard immediately.,b:Grasp the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and allow the car to slow gradually.,c:Rapidly pump the brake pedal.,d:Turn sharply to the side of the road.
note: Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, avoid heavy braking, and pull off safely when possible.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, which action is recommended?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Brake hard and immediately steer to the shoulder.
note: For a sudden blowout, grasp the wheel, ease off the gas, slow gradually and move out of the traffic lane once safe to do so; avoid heavy braking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should a driver approach right-of-way rules in traffic?
options: a:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way to avoid collisions.,b:Assume all other drivers will obey right-of-way rules.,c:Assume most drivers obey the rules.
note: Do not assume others will follow the rules — be ready to yield when necessary to prevent crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When another vehicle is passing you, how should you respond?
options: a:Brake hard to prevent being passed.,b:Maintain a steady speed and position.,c:Speed up to block the pass.
note: When being passed, keep a steady speed and allow the passing vehicle to safely complete the maneuver; do not speed up or obstruct them.

question: Which driving skills are impaired by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Alertness.,b:Coordination.,c:Both alertness and coordination are affected.
note: Alcohol and many drugs negatively affect alertness, coordination, reaction time, and concentration, reducing driving safety.

question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:After you have passed the other vehicle’s front bumper.,b:When you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.,c:When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: Return to your lane only after you can see both headlights of the overtaken vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: What do double solid yellow centerlines on the roadway mean about passing?
options: a:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed from both directions.,c:Passing only allowed from your direction.,d:Passing allowed only during daylight.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit crossing the centerline to pass from either direction.

question: What is a common problem caused by continuous hard braking on ice or snow?
options: a:It helps you stop faster.,b:It can lock the wheels and cause loss of steering.,c:It keeps brakes from freezing.,d:It improves traction.
note: Hard continuous braking on slippery surfaces can lock wheels and cause loss of steering control.

question: How much following distance should you maintain for every 10 mph of speed?
options: a:One car length for every 10 mph.,b:One-half car length for every 10 mph.,c:Three car lengths for every 10 mph.,d:Two car lengths for every 10 mph.
note: Allow at least one car length of space for every 10 mph of your speed to provide adequate stopping distance.

question: If the center of a multilane road has a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line, what does that mean?
options: a:Passing is allowed from the side with the solid line.,b:Passing is allowed only from the side next to the dashed line.,c:Passing is prohibited in both directions.,d:Both sides may pass.
note: When a dashed yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, only traffic next to the dashed line may cross to pass when safe.

question: Before entering an intersection, what sequence should you use to look for hazards?
options: a:Look left, then right, then left again.,b:Look only to your left.,c:Look only to your right.
note: Check both directions and look left again because traffic from the left will be closer than from the right.

question: Why should you signal continuously while making a turn?
options: a:It lets other road users know your intentions.,b:It is illegal to turn off your signal early.,c:It always shortens travel time.,d:It makes the turn safer even if not needed.
note: Signal early and continuously so other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians understand your intentions.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas of the roadway that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.,b:Traffic control devices.,c:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in your mirrors; always check over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: What is a likely consequence of tailgating other drivers?
options: a:It can provoke and frustrate other drivers.,b:It cannot result in a traffic citation.,c:It helps prevent being cut off and reduces collisions.
note: Tailgating increases the risk of collisions and may lead to aggressive responses; it is unsafe and may be illegal.

question: If a pedestrian is crossing your lane where there is no marked crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Make eye contact and then pass.,b:Slow down briefly as you pass.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,d:Signal and proceed normally.
note: Even without a crosswalk, you must yield to pedestrians crossing your lane and let them finish crossing.

question: When should you increase the gap between your vehicle and the one ahead?
options: a:When you are being tailgated by another driver.,b:When following a small passenger vehicle.,c:When driving more slowly than the posted speed.
note: If someone is tailgating you, create extra space ahead of your vehicle and avoid sudden braking or stops.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct immediate response?
options: a:Ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.,b:Brake as hard as possible until the skid stops.,c:Turn off the ignition immediately.
note: Take your foot off the accelerator and steer into the skid; do not brake hard unless you have ABS, which requires different technique.

question: Is it legal to drive while taking medication that impairs your driving?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If prescribed by a doctor.,c:If you do not feel drowsy.
note: Driving while impaired by any substance, including prescription or over-the-counter drugs that affect your abilities, is illegal and unsafe.

question: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent has what effect on crash risk?
options: a:It roughly doubles your chances of being in a fatal crash.,b:It will not have any effect on your driving.,c:It will not put other drivers at risk.
note: Even small increases in BAC significantly increase the risk of a serious crash; impairment begins at low levels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you intend to pass another vehicle, what is a safe assumption?
options: a:Do not assume the other driver will make space for you to return.,b:Assume the other driver will let you back in if you signal.,c:Assume the other driver will maintain a constant speed.
note: Never assume other drivers will yield space; ensure you can return safely to your lane before passing.

question: If you drive more slowly than the flow of traffic, you will most likely:
options: a:Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.,b:Improve traffic flow.,c:Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.
note: Driving significantly slower than the normal flow can impede traffic and may lead to a citation.

question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended for driving with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
options: a:0.15 percent or more.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:Any amount.
note: Mississippi has zero tolerance for drivers under 21; any detectable amount of alcohol can lead to license suspension.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.,b:Signal and pull into the slow lane.,c:Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.
note: If possible get the vehicle off the roadway, turn on emergency flashers, and make sure it is visible to other drivers.

question: When are large trucks likely to lose speed and create a hazard for following vehicles?
options: a:When driving up long or steep hills.,b:When driving down long, gradual hills.,c:When driving through long, gradual curves.
note: Trucks lose speed climbing long or steep grades; allow extra space and be patient when passing.

question: How should a driver check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Glance over the appropriate shoulder to check the blind spot.,b:Only use the left outside mirror.,c:Rely solely on the inside rearview mirror.,d:Assume mirrors show all areas.
note: Look over your shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter to confirm no vehicle is there.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Passing is prohibited in both directions.,b:The right-hand lane may pass.,c:Both lanes may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposite-direction traffic and prohibit passing for drivers in either direction.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:Because motorcycles do not obey traffic laws.,b:Because motorcycles can stop much more quickly than a typical vehicle.,c:Because motorcycles always drive slower than cars.
note: Motorcycles can stop faster than many vehicles; following too closely reduces your time to react and increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before a turn should you signal your intention to turn?
options: a:At least 100 feet before beginning the turn.,b:About 50 feet before the turn.,c:About 10 feet before the turn.
note: Signal at least 100 feet in advance (or as required by law) so other road users know your intentions.

question: As daylight begins to fade, which lights should you use to help others see you?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: Turn on your low beam headlights as visibility decreases to make your vehicle more visible to others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, what is your responsibility?
options: a:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Expect oncoming traffic to yield to you.,c:Complete the turn without yielding if you have a green light.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic going straight and to pedestrians in the crosswalk before turning.

question: At a railroad crossing you must:
options: a:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings (school buses, trucks carrying hazardous materials, etc.).,b:Watch for multiple trains.,c:Both of the above.
note: Exercise extreme caution at crossings: be aware that some vehicles are required to stop and that more than one train may be approaching.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving an alley or driveway and crossing a sidewalk to enter the street, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed if no pedestrians are visible.,b:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk area.,c:Expect pedestrians to yield to you.
note: You must stop before entering a sidewalk or sidewalk area when leaving a driveway or alley and yield to pedestrians and traffic.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection instruct you to do?
options: a:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you should reduce speed and proceed with caution; you do not have to come to a full stop unless necessary.

question: To prevent hydroplaning in rainy weather, what should you do?
options: a:Decrease your speed.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.,d:Drive in the center of the lane only.
note: Lower your speed in rain to reduce the chance of tires losing contact with the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a Yield sign, you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.,b:Yield the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.,c:Always slow down and proceed without stopping.
note: Slow or stop if necessary at a yield sign and give the right-of-way to any traffic close enough to cause conflict.

question: Which road area is most likely to remain icy in cold, wet weather?
options: a:A hilly open road.,b:A residential street.,c:A shaded section of roadway.
note: Shaded areas freeze sooner and thaw later than the rest of the road and are more likely to be icy after precipitation.

question: What should you do to reduce glare from an oncoming vehicle's headlights?
options: a:Glance briefly toward the right side of the road, then resume looking ahead.,b:Keep your focus fixed on the centerline.,c:Flash your high beams to warn the other driver.
note: Glancing to the right edge of the lane helps avoid direct glare while you monitor the vehicle’s position.

question: Which behavior could identify an aggressive driver?
options: a:Frequent, erratic, or improper lane changes.,b:Driving slowly below the speed limit.,c:Having many passengers in the vehicle.
note: Aggressive drivers often make unsafe lane changes and other erratic maneuvers; if you encounter one, get out of their way.
